RELEASE · V1.0.0-RC.105 · DRAFT

RC.105: BETTER RANKING ON LONG PAGES
AND CJK TEXT.

XERJ ENGINEERING · DRAFT FOR REVIEW

rc.105 is about finding the right passage. A long page no longer outranks the page that answers your question. Chinese text is searched in a way that fits the language. A top-10 over a field with more than 100,000 distinct values comes back with exact counts. Hybrid search reads less, and a merge holds less in memory.

XERJ is an AI-native search engine. It also speaks the Elasticsearch 8.x API, so an existing client works on day one. Many fixes in this release make that API answer the way such a client expects.

01 · LONG PAGES

The page that answers ranks first

BM25 compares the length of a field with the average length. XERJ stored that length in one byte, and the byte stopped growing at 1,690 tokens. Every longer field was scored as if it were 1,690 tokens long, while the average used the true lengths. Long pages looked short, and they outranked the page that answered the query.

New segments now store the real length. On a medical reference of 121 pages and 1,993 questions, searched on title and content, the right page came first more often:

64.78
recall at 1, was 56.60
The page that holds the answer is the first hit.
81.74
recall at 3, was 76.77
The page that holds the answer is in the top 3.

On public benchmarks with short documents, the change is small. With a plain multi_match, SciFact nDCG@10 went from 0.6572 to 0.6537, and NFCorpus from 0.3016 to 0.3020. With the query that xerj search sends, SciFact went from 0.6550 to 0.6552, and NFCorpus from 0.3058 to 0.3087.

02 · CJK

Chinese text, searched by bigrams

When at least 20% of the letters in a dataset's text are Han, kana or Hangul, xerj autoindex now gives the index the xerj_cjk analyzer. It splits the text into pairs of characters, and it folds Traditional Han to Simplified, so a question in one script finds a passage in the other. Text with kana gets the plain cjk analyzer. English text keeps its stemmer.

The cjk tokenizer also splits non-CJK words on word boundaries and drops punctuation. revenue, is now revenue, and a full-width comma is no longer a token. Short Chinese, Japanese and Korean bodies without spaces are now mapped as text, so they are searchable after autoindex.

On a corpus of 29 statute files and 20 law questions, the passage that holds the answer moved up:

0.95
recall at 1, was 0.45
Questions in Simplified Chinese.
1.00
recall at 3, was 0.60
Questions in Simplified Chinese.
0.90
recall at 1, was 0.65
The same questions in Traditional Chinese.
0.95
recall at 3, was 0.80
The same questions in Traditional Chinese.

English results did not change: the medical reference above gave the same ranks. A mapping that names cjk by hand keeps the unfolded behaviour.

03 · EXACT TOP-N

A top-10 over 100,000 keys, with exact counts

A terms aggregation over user IDs or IP addresses can see many distinct values. Earlier builds kept the first 65,536 keys in document order, and the count of the other documents was wrong. search.max_buckets now counts the buckets a search returns, not the keys it sees.

Over 100,000 distinct keys, terms size: 10 now answers 200, with sum_other_doc_count 99,991. A request fails with a 400 too_many_buckets_exception only when the buckets it keeps are more than the limit. This works on one index and across indices. The search.max_buckets cluster setting now also moves the engine's own cap.

04 · FASTER

Hybrid search reads only the page you get

A hybrid query has a BM25 leg and a kNN leg. Both legs now return ids and scores only. XERJ fuses them, and then reads _source for the documents on the returned page, and no others. The pages are the same as before: ids, order, scores and _source matched on every page we compared, 3,120 pages over two datasets.

4.31 ms
was 7.20 ms
Hybrid, size 10, 3,000 documents with 768-dimension vectors.
6.29 ms
was 8.80 ms
Hybrid, size 10, 5,000 documents, kNN on HNSW.

With the vector left out of _source, the 3,000-document case went from 5.09 to 3.35 ms. The 5,000-document case did not get faster. XERJ_HYBRID_DEFER_SOURCE=0 brings back the old reads.

Searches also stop waiting on disk while bulk writes run. A flush, a _bulk and WAL maintenance used to hold the index's publish lock through fsyncs. They no longer do. The same fsyncs still happen, so durability does not change. With a writer running, p99 over all reads went from 204-265 ms to 40-85 ms, and the writer went from 34-50k to 53-66k documents per second.

A match_all page decoded a whole segment for each hit when the cache had no room. On a 504k-document index, the zero-hit hint took 47-52 s. Each segment is now read once per page, and the hint takes 0.7-0.9 s.

05 · LESS MEMORY

Merges and flushes hold less

Some fields are a scalar in one document and an array in the next, such as "t1" and ["t1","t2"]. A merge or flush used to parse each such row into a tree of values. It now keeps the row as JSON text. The bytes written are the same.

398.9 MB
peak heap, was 725.3 MB
One 6,000-document encode with a 1024-dimension vector and mixed fields.
791-820 MB
peak RSS, was 936-943 MB
A 12,000-document _forcemerge under a 1,200 MB process cap.

Under the automatic memory cap, that merge peaked at the same level both ways. Data without mixed fields sees no difference.

_forcemerge now respects the process memory cap. On 84,600 documents with a 1024-dimension vector, the peak at an 8 GiB cap went from 4,751 and 4,919 MB to 4,204 and 4,285 MB. At a 4 GiB cap, the old build went past the cap to 4,248 MB. The new one stops at 4,014 MB and answers 429, and the index keeps every segment and document. A client that drops the connection no longer cancels the merge half way. A merge that is still making progress does not get a 429.

A flush near the memory watermark used to return freed pages to the operating system inline, for 64-133 ms at p90. That work now runs on its own thread, and the flush spends under 0.12 ms there at p90.

06 · CORRECTNESS

Answers that match what a client expects

The release gate is the Elasticsearch YAML conformance suite: a release is cut only when it reports zero failures. These are the fixes in rc.105 that change what you see:

  • Keyword normalizers. A keyword field can use lowercase, or a custom normalizer built from lowercase, uppercase, asciifolding and trim. With lowercase and asciifolding, term foo: "BAR" finds "BÀR" and "bar". Any other normalizer is refused with a 400 and the reason, instead of being accepted and ignored.
  • * field patterns search typed fields. Native q, multi_match on * and a field-less query_string now match numbers, booleans, dates and IP addresses when the value parses for that field.
  • Object sub-fields get their own full-text index. meta.note is indexed under its own path with its own analyzer, and ranked by BM25 on new segments.
  • Keyword multi-fields match by whole value. match title.raw: "World" no longer hits "Hello World", before or after a flush.
  • Stable ties. function_score with field_value_factor breaks ties by arrival order on every path. A filter-only bool scores 0.0 before a flush too.
  • Clear errors. A wrong-type value on a boolean, IP or date field, a field_value_factor on a document without the field, a point-in-time search that also names an index, and collapse.inner_hits without a name are now refused with a 400 and the reason.
  • Local nodes. Every node a client starts leads its own session, so closing a terminal does not stop it. A call no longer waits 120 s for a node that is shutting down. xerj autoindex --no-graph migrates an old journal in place instead of stopping.
07 · UPGRADE NOTES

Before you upgrade

  • Back up your data folder. rc.105 writes field lengths in a new form. A binary older than rc.105 refuses those files instead of misreading them, so once rc.105 has written a segment, you cannot go back without the backup.
  • Reindex to get the new ranking. Segments written before rc.105 keep their old lengths until they are reindexed. Existing indices keep their analyzer, so run xerj autoindex again with a fresh prefix and state directory to get xerj_cjk on Chinese text. Older segments of object fields keep answering from stored documents, and the next merge rebuilds them.
  • Some requests that answered 200 now answer 400. A normalizer other than the supported ones. A wrong-type value on a boolean, IP or date field, unless lenient is on. A field_value_factor that scores a document without the field: set missing to keep the old ranking. A point-in-time search that names an index. An unnamed collapse.inner_hits.
  • Some result sets change. * patterns now reach number, boolean, date and IP fields. A keyword sub-field matches by whole value, so multi_match "fruit" no longer matches meta.tag: "Fruit".
  • A terms aggregation over many keys now succeeds. A request fails only when the buckets it returns are more than search.max_buckets.

09 · INSTALL

Install v1.0.0-rc.105

The installers download a GitHub release and check its SHA-256. Pin this release with XERJ_VERSION. On Linux, macOS, and Windows Git Bash, MSYS, and Cygwin:

$ curl -fsSL https://xerj.org/get | XERJ_VERSION=v1.0.0-rc.105 sh
$ export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
$ xerj --version

On Windows PowerShell, open a new terminal after it:

> $env:XERJ_VERSION='v1.0.0-rc.105'; irm https://xerj.org/get.ps1 | iex

Re-run the installer you used last time. xerj --version should print v1.0.0-rc.105. The longer matrix and the manual checksum are on the install page.
